## Highlights
### New
- On iPhone and iPad, a New Tab button floats at the bottom of the sidebar beside the sidebar button, so a new tab is always a tap away.
### Improved
- Pages show their loading progress as a stronger fill in the address field, and the thin loading line along the top of the page on Mac is gone. - Browser windows on Mac resize much smaller, so two fit side by side on a laptop screen, and the pinned tabs keep their place in a short window. - On iPhone Duo held upright, the page and Space controls move into the bar across the top, leaving the sidebar more room, and the controls that don't fit fold into a menu, Settings first. Back and Forward always show on iPhone and iPad, dimmed until there is somewhere to go.
### Fixed
- Switching between Sub-Spaces that show the same pinned tab keeps its page on screen instead of leaving it blank, and with extensions pinned, the pinned tabs stay still as you switch. - Zooming a page out on iPhone and iPad fits it to the window instead of leaving a blank band down the side. - On iPhone Duo held upright, the controls stay in the top bar while the keyboard is open.

## Highlights
### Fixed
- Downloads follow the Automatic Downloads choice of the site you’re on, including files it serves from another address, such as GitHub release files. A blocked download’s message no longer appears twice. - Chromium pages use your default zoom when they open and keep your chosen zoom as you navigate. - Chromium is updated to 154.0.8037.57 with upstream security and compatibility fixes.
